notes: On 14 December 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at their hideout in a forest in Emohua LGA (Rivers) and rescued four abductees. Two members of the group were killed.
On 4 September 2021, a soldier opened fire while trying to disperse a crowd during local elections in Gwanki (Makarfi LGA, Kaduna). A girl was killed by a stray bullet.

On 13 March 2023, policemen attached to Operation Whirl Punch engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash, after the militia blocked the Galadimawa-Tumbruku road (Giwa, Kaduna). One militia member was killed, others fled with bullet wounds and the policemen recovered one rifle and two live rounds of ammunition.
Looting: On 26 December 2023, ISWAP raided and looted drugs from a Primary Health Care center in Mainok (Kaga, Borno).
On 5 August 2024, the Buccaneers and Eiye clashed and killed one person in Ake Junction, Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun).

On 23 October 2020, Nigerian police forces attacked a journalist in Udu LGA, Delta over the enforcement of the state-wide curfew despite the journalist being on an official assignment. No reported fatalities.

Security measures: On 23 January 2024, the governor of Plateau state imposed a 24 hour curfew on Mangu LGA (Plateau) following violence which broke out in different parts of the town [coded separately].

On 15 February 2024, a Naval officer shot and killed a man at a military checkpoint at Owerri-Nta (Isiala Ngwa South, Abia) after he refused to stop at the checkpoint. The Navy claimed that the victim was shot because he was struggling for a gun with the soldier after he was invited over an allegation of theft levelled against him.

On 12 January 2024, the Nigerian police arrested a Kaduna militia's kingpin around the Abuja-Kaduna Road flyover by Rido Junction, coded to Rido (Chikun, Kaduna). The kingpin was responsible for many high-profile attacks and abductions in the area. The police recovered forty- eight AK-47 rifles from him.

On 10 March 2024, an unidentified armed group numbering six abducted a Chinese national from a guest house around Eyenkorin in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara) where he was lodged. The police claimed to have arrested three suspects in connection with the abduction. The abductee was rescued on 19 March by operatives of the state police command (there are no further details on ransom payment or a clash).

On 29 July 2022, an unidentified armed group abducted a gold miner and his driver along Ilesa-Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded for the miner, the victims were released around 8 August after 20 million naira was paid as ransom.

On 18 December 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the police orderly of a high court judge, then proceeded to abduct the judge and her driver as they were traveling along Okobo axis of Oron-Uyo road (Oron, Akwa Ibom). The assailants had posed as a local defense militia on the road. The abductees were released on 23 December, there are no reports on ransom payment.
On 4 October 2021, unidentified armed men shot sporadically while enforcing a sit at home order in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). Casualties unknown. Police sources denied reports of the attack.

On 17 September 2024, the Nigerian troops clashed with a Kaduna militia, killing two in an ambush at Hayin Nakwakina village in Giwa LGA, coded to Hayin Kanwa (Giwa, Kaduna). The troops recovered two motorcycles, a mobile phone, and machetes.
On 14 August 2024, the Aye (Black Axe) and the Eiye clashed and killed one person at Oki Olodo (Lagelu, Oyo).

On 21 April 2023, Nigerian troops clashed with suspected IPOB militants when they raided their camps within 9th Mile (Udi, Enugu) and Nkanu East LGA [coded separately]. One militant was killed, 7 others were arrested, the makeshift camps were destroyed and other items were recovered. Fatality split across 2 events, coded to 0.
On 7 July 2022, the Nigerian Airforce accidentally killed one person and injured 13 others in an air strike targeting some camps of militiamen in Kunkuna (Safana, Katsina). 1 fatality reported.

Around 13 February 2022 (as reported), Nigerian troops carried out airstrikes against ISWAP camps in Tumbun Kaiyowa (Abadan, Borno), Tumbun Madayi, Tumbun Allura, Parisu and Njimia [coded separately]. Five militant leaders were killed in the strikes across the locations, five fatalities split across five events, coded as 1.
On 13 May 2021, an unidentified armed group attacked Moniokoro police station Rumuola (Obio, Rivers). Casualties unknown.

On 9 September 2021, gunmen engaged police officers in an armed clash that led to the killing of three police officers and the abduction of an unspecified number of expatriates in Akukutoru LGA (Rivers) coded as Abonnema. The abducted expatriates were released around 4 October.
